best_architecture: Recommended pattern: SEPARATE the serving engine from Unsloth, and select the engine by workload. Use Unsloth (FastLanguageModel/FastModel.from_pretrained) for FINE-TUNING and one-off / single-stream generation, NOT as the production multi-user inference server. Unsloth has no continuous batching and no PagedAttention, so under concurrency its throughput collapses; it is a training/LoRA toolkit that requires extra steps to deploy. For the Local-Claw single-A6000 (48GB) autonomous-agent workload, the strongest architecture is: (1) Quantize/fine-tune the brain model with Unsloth + bitsandbytes (NF4 4-bit, double quantization) or export an Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 GGUF; (2) SERVE through a real inference engine. Two viable serving tiers: (a) vLLM with a GPTQ/AWQ (or Unsloth dynamic-4bit / FP8) checkpoint when you need OpenAI-compatible HTTP, continuous batching, PagedAttention KV-cache paging, and hot-swappable LoRA adapters for multiple concurrent skill workers; (b) llama.cpp/Ollama with an Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 GGUF (Q4_K_M class) when you want simplest single-box deployment and the best accuracy-per-byte for tool calling. For the brain (Gemma, MoE, ~4-bit) plus a Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fallback, do NOT try to co-resident both at full precision on one 48GB card: a 32B model at 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ is ~16-18GB of weights, leaving ~25-30GB for KV cache + activations + framework overhead + the skill workers. Budget KV cache explicitly: GPTQ/AWQ quantize weights only, KV cache stays FP16 and scales with context * batch, and is the usual OOM trigger on long agent traces — set vLLM --max-model-len and --gpu-memory-utilization (e.g. 0.80-0.85) conservatively, enable KV-cache quantization (FP8 KV) if available, and reserve VRAM headroom for the embedding model (Chroma) and any GPU-side skill workers. Strategy: keep ONE model resident as the primary brain via vLLM, treat the 32B coder as a swap-in fallback (load on demand or run on a second process/GPU), rather than holding both simultaneously. For STREAMING in the TS-MCP-server + Python-MCP-client design: if serving via vLLM/Ollama, consume their native OpenAI-compatible streaming (SSE) endpoint — do not hand-roll TextIteratorStreamer. Only if you call transformers/Unsloth directly should you bridge generation to FastAPI: run model.generate() in a background threading.Thread with transformers.TextIteratorStreamer(skip_prompt=True, skip_special_tokens=True, timeout=...), then yield tokens from the iterator inside a FastAPI StreamingResponse / sse_starlette EventSourceResponse with media_type text/event-stream and headers Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no. The Thread is required because generate() is blocking/synchronous and would otherwise stall the asyncio event loop. For tool-call accuracy prefer Unsloth Dynamic quants (dynamic per-layer bit-width, imatrix calibrated on chat + tool-calling data) over naive uniform Q4_0; naive Q4_0 measurably degrades real-world / tool-calling accuracy. Chat-template handling: ALWAYS render via tokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., tools=[...]) for the exact model variant rather than concatenating strings, and ensure the serving engine uses the matching Jinja template + tool-call parser (e.g. vLLM --enable-auto-tool-choice with the correct --tool-call-parser, or llama.cpp --jinja); a mismatched parser leaves the OpenAI tool_calls field empty and dumps raw tool-call tokens into message.content. [uncertain] Gemma-version specifics: Gemma 3 uses pythonic-style function calling (vLLM PR #17149 adds tool_chat_template_gemma3_pythonic.jinja for --tool-call-parser pythonic); a distinct 'Gemma 4' native token-based tool-call format (<|tool_call>...<tool_call|>) is referenced in some sources but is NOT independently verifiable as of 2026-06, so treat any Gemma-4-MoE / 26B-A4B 4-bit details as provisional and validate against the actual released model card before committing the spec.
reference_papers: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs (Dettmers et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.14314 - introduces 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), double quantization, and paged optimizers; basis for Unsloth's bitsandbytes 4-bit loading; finetunes a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU

Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (Kwon et al. 2023, SOSP'23) - arxiv:2309.06180 - the PagedAttention algorithm and vLLM; near-zero KV-cache waste, 2-4x throughput over prior systems; core to the multi-user serving recommendation
FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness (Dao et al. 2022, NeurIPS 35) - arxiv:2205.14135 - IO-aware exact attention kernels used by both Unsloth and vLLM
FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning (Dao 2023) - arxiv:2307.08691 - improved attention kernel parallelism relevant to A6000-class serving
GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers (Frantar et al. 2022) - arxiv:2210.17323 - layer-by-layer 4-bit PTQ format supported by vLLM

AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration (Lin et al. 2023, MLSys'24) - arxiv:2306.00978 - protects salient weights; preferred 4-bit format for vLLM/SGLang GPU serving

vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention (Prabhu et al. 2024) - arxiv:2405.04437 - alternative KV-cache memory management; relevant context for KV-cache budgeting [uncertain]

Bench360: Benchmarking Local LLM Inference from 360 Degrees (2025) - arxiv:2511.16682 - local-inference benchmarking across engines; useful for engine selection but recency/details unverified [uncertain]
reference_repos: unslothai/unsloth - FastLanguageModel/FastModel.from_pretrained, dynamic 4-bit quant, LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning, GGUF export; load_in_4bit=True and optional fast_inference (vLLM-backed) - https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth

vllm-project/vllm - high-throughput PagedAttention serving engine; OpenAI-compatible API, continuous batching, LoRA hot-swap, GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF/FP8 support; primary recommended serving layer for multi-user Local-Claw - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm

vllm-project/vllm PR #17149 - adds Gemma 3 pythonic-style function-calling Jinja chat template (tool_chat_template_gemma3_pythonic.jinja) usable with --tool-call-parser pythonic - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/17149
ggml-org/llama.cpp - GGUF inference engine with native Gemma support and tool calling via --jinja; pairs with Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 GGUF quants - https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
artidoro/qlora - reference QLoRA implementation (NF4 + bitsandbytes + PEFT) - https://github.com/artidoro/qlora
bitsandbytes-foundation/bitsandbytes - 4-bit NF4/FP4 quantization backend used by Unsloth and transformers - https://github.com/bitsandbytes-foundation/bitsandbytes
huggingface/transformers - AutoModelForCausalLM, TextIteratorStreamer, tokenizer.apply_chat_template(tools=...) for chat-template + tool rendering - https://github.com/huggingface/transformers

fastapi/fastapi Discussion #9407 - canonical pattern for bridging HuggingFace TextIteratorStreamer to FastAPI StreamingResponse with a background Thread - https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/9407
sysmon/sse-starlette (sse_starlette) - EventSourceResponse for clean SSE streaming from FastAPI - https://github.com/sysid/sse-starlette
unsloth/gemma-*-GGUF (Hugging Face) - Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 GGUF releases for Gemma; verify exact Gemma version/variant against the released model card - https://huggingface.co/unsloth [uncertain]
key_libraries: unsloth (Python, >=2025.x) - FastLanguageModel/FastModel loading, dynamic 4-bit quant, QLoRA fine-tuning, GGUF export; brain-model quantization/fine-tuning

vllm (Python, >=0.6.x; check current at deploy) - production serving engine: PagedAttention, continuous batching, OpenAI-compatible server, LoRA serving, AWQ/GPTQ/GGUF/FP8; primary multi-user inference layer
bitsandbytes (Python, >=0.43.x) - NF4/FP4 4-bit quantization + double quantization backend for Unsloth/transformers
transformers (Python, >=4.44.x) - model/tokenizer abstractions, TextIteratorStreamer, apply_chat_template(tools=...) for Gemma/Qwen chat templates and tool rendering
peft (Python) - LoRA/QLoRA adapter implementation used under Unsloth for fine-tuning the brain model
accelerate (Python) - device placement / mixed-precision (bf16 on A6000) helper used by Unsloth and transformers
torch (Python, >=2.3, CUDA 12.x) - underlying tensor/runtime; use bfloat16 on A6000 (Gemma has FP16 overflow issues, A6000 supports bf16)
fastapi (Python) + uvicorn - HTTP layer for the streaming bridge if calling models directly (StreamingResponse)
sse-starlette (Python) - EventSourceResponse for SSE-formatted token streaming
flash-attn (Python, flash-attention 2) - optional fused attention kernels for faster A6000/H100 generation
llama-cpp-python / llama.cpp (C++/Python binding) - alternative GGUF serving path for Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 quants with --jinja tool calling
autoawq / auto-gptq (Python) - produce AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit checkpoints for vLLM when not using Unsloth dynamic-4bit or GGUF [uncertain]
